chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi ʿUmayr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abi ʿAbdillah عليه السلام, who said:

A woman came and lodged a complaint against a Bedouin who had terrified her, causing her to miscarry her fetus. The Bedouin said, “It did not cry out, nor did it make a sound, and the like of it is disregarded without compensation.” So the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “Be silent, rhyming speaker. Upon you is a ghurrah: a servant youth, male or female.”

key_terms.أَفْزَعَهَا: terrified her and caused shock or fear
key_terms.جَنِينًا: a fetus cast from the womb
key_terms.غُرَّةٌ: the prescribed compensation for a miscarried fetus
key_terms.يُطَلُّ: to be left uncompensated or deemed without blood-compensation
key_terms.ٱسْتَعْدَتْ: sought redress or lodged a complaint before an authority

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone causes a pregnant woman to miscarry by frightening her?
ai.summary: This hadith states the ruling concerning a person who frightens a pregnant woman and causes her to miscarry. The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم imposed financial liability for the lost fetus, establishing compensation even if the fetus did not cry or show signs of life after expulsion.
